'''Sauerbrey:''' {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Parris Glendening]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Parris Glendening]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsMD}} The '''1998 Maryland gubernatorial election''' was held on November 3, 1998 to elect the [[Governor of Maryland|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Maryland|lieutenant governor of Maryland]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Parris Glendening]] was re-elected to a second term in office over Ellen Sauerbrey in a rematch of the [[1994 Maryland gubernatorial election|1994 election]]. Glendening defeated Sauerbrey by a much larger margin than he had in 1994.{{Cite web |title=Sauerbrey aides say discrepancies prove vote fraud |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/1994/12/16/sauerbrey-aides-say-discrepancies-prove-vote-fraud/ |access-date=2022-12-15 |website=Baltimore Sun}} Glendening easily won the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] primary after defeating several candidates. Sauerbrey also easily won her party's nomination. Despite the controversial nature of the previous election, Governor Glendening comfortably beat back Sauerbrey's spirited challenge, winning his second and final term as governor. {{asof|2024}}, this was the last time that [[Allegany County, Maryland|Allegany County]] voted Democratic in a gubernatorial election and the last time that the lieutenant gubernatorial nominee of the winning ticket was not a person of color. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== *Lawrence K.
